title: 3-Day NYC Itinerary (First Timers): Manhattan essentials — Central Park, Times Square, Brooklyn Bridge, museums, pizza, and nightlife in a tight 3-day plan.
description: Your first time in New York City is a sensory overload in the best way possible. This 3-day itinerary covers the iconic highlights — the Statue of Liberty, Central Park, Times Square at night, the Brooklyn Bridge at golden hour — while leaving room for the city's legendary food scene. Dollar pizza at 2am, a perfect bagel for breakfast, cheesecake that lives up to the hype. You'll ride the subway like a New Yorker by day two.

days.neighborhoods: Battery Park · Financial District · 9/11 Memorial · Brooklyn Bridge
days.title: Lower Manhattan & the Statue of Liberty
days.description: Start with the icons — the Statue of Liberty, the 9/11 Memorial, and the Brooklyn Bridge at sunset. Lower Manhattan packs the most emotional punch of any neighborhood in the city.

activities.name: Bagel Breakfast at Leo's Bagels
activities.description: Start your NYC trip the right way — with a proper New York bagel. Leo's in the Financial District makes them fresh, boiled-then-baked in the traditional style. Get an everything bagel with scallion cream cheese. Take the first ferry from Battery Park (9am departure — arrive by 8:30am for security). Visit Ellis Island first for the Immigration Museum with fewer crowds, then Liberty Island. The whole circuit takes about 3-4 hours. Even if you don't go up into the crown, the views of Manhattan from the water are spectacular.
details: ⏰ Opens 7am — get there early to beat the line
📍 Battery Park, Castle Clinton departure point
💲 $24.50 reserve ticket (includes ferry + both islands + audio tour)
💡 Crown access ($24.50 extra) sells out months ahead — the pedestal access is more realistic for most visitors
tips: Don't buy tickets from anyone on the street in Battery Park. Statue City Cruises (statuecruises.com) is the only legitimate operator.

activities.name: 9/11 Memorial & Museum
activities.description: Walk from Battery Park through the Financial District to the 9/11 Memorial — the twin reflecting pools where the towers stood. The memorial plaza is free and deeply moving. The underground museum ($29) is one of the most powerful museum experiences in the world, but be prepared emotionally — give yourself at least 2 hours. A quick walk through the Financial District past the New York Stock Exchange, Federal Hall (where George Washington was inaugurated), and the famous Charging Bull sculpture on Broadway. It's a 15-minute photo-op detour, not an all-day affair.
details: 💡 The Fearless Girl statue has moved to the NYSE entrance

activities.name: Walk the Brooklyn Bridge at Sunset
activities.description: Time your Brooklyn Bridge walk for golden hour — the views of Lower Manhattan with the sun setting behind it are some of the most photographed in the world. Start from the Manhattan side (entrance near City Hall) and walk the mile across to DUMBO on the Brooklyn side. Once you're in Brooklyn, explore DUMBO (Down Under the Manhattan Bridge Overpass). Walk to the famous Washington Street photo spot where the Empire State Building is perfectly framed by the Manhattan Bridge arch. Then stroll along Brooklyn Bridge Park's waterfront with Manhattan's skyline glittering across the river.
details: 📍 Brooklyn Bridge pedestrian entrance near City Hall
⏰ Walk takes 30-45 minutes — start about an hour before sunset
💡 Jane's Carousel in the park is a beautifully restored 1922 carousel ($2/ride)
tips: After Juliana's, walk to Pebble Beach in Brooklyn Bridge Park for a nighttime skyline view. It's one of the best free views in the city.

days.neighborhoods: Central Park · Rockefeller Center · Times Square · Broadway
days.title: Midtown & Central Park
days.description: The heart of Manhattan — a morning in Central Park, world-class art at the Met, sunset views from Top of the Rock, and a Broadway show to cap the night.

activities.name: Central Park Morning Walk
activities.description: Start your day with a walk through Central Park — 843 acres of green space in the middle of Manhattan. Enter at the southeast corner (59th & 5th Ave) and walk through The Mall, Bethesda Terrace and Fountain (the most photographed spot in the park), and Bow Bridge. In April, the cherry blossoms along the Bridle Path and around the Reservoir are in full bloom. The Met is one of the greatest art museums on Earth — 5,000 years of art spanning every culture and continent. With only a couple of hours, hit the highlights: the Egyptian Temple of Dendur, the European Paintings galleries (Vermeer, Monet, Van Gogh), and the rooftop garden with Central Park views. Don't try to see everything — you literally can't in one visit.
details: 📍 Enter at Grand Army Plaza (59th & 5th Ave)
⏰ 2-3 hours for a good exploration of the southern half
tips: The Met's pay-what-you-wish policy is only for NY/NJ/CT residents. Everyone else pays the $30 entry fee — but it's worth every penny.

activities.name: 5th Avenue & St. Patrick's Cathedral
activities.description: Walk down 5th Avenue from the Met — you'll pass some of the world's most famous shops (Tiffany's, Saks, Bergdorf Goodman). Stop at St. Patrick's Cathedral, a stunning Neo-Gothic church that's free to enter. Even if you're not religious, the vaulted ceilings and rose window are breathtaking. Book a sunset time slot at Rockefeller Center's observation deck. At 70 stories up, you get a 360-degree view of Manhattan — Central Park to the north, the Empire State Building to the south, and the Hudson River to the west. Most New Yorkers agree: this is the best observation deck in the city.
details: ⏰ Book sunset time (around 7pm in April) at topoftherocknyc.com

activities.name: Times Square
activities.description: Love it or hate it, Times Square at night is something every first-time visitor should experience once. The sensory overload of neon lights, massive billboards, and crowds from every corner of the world is uniquely New York. Walk through, take your photos, soak it in — then get out. Don't eat here (tourist trap prices, mediocre food). Seeing a Broadway show is a quintessential NYC experience. Current hits include The Great Gatsby, Hamilton, Wicked, and The Outsiders. For last-minute discount tickets, try the TKTS booth in Times Square (up to 50% off same-day shows) or the TodayTix app. Show up an hour early for the best selection.
details: ⏰ 20-30 minutes is plenty. Visit after dark for full effect.
📍 Theater District, 41st–54th Streets between 6th and 8th Avenues
💡 TKTS booth opens at 3pm for evening shows — the line is long but moves fast
tips: If you can't get Broadway tickets, Off-Broadway shows are often just as good. Sleep No More, Stomp, and Blue Man Group are all fantastic.

days.neighborhoods: Greenwich Village · Chelsea · High Line · SoHo · Little Italy
days.title: Museums, Greenwich Village & the High Line
days.description: Explore the neighborhoods that give NYC its soul — bohemian Greenwich Village, the elevated High Line park, foodie haven Chelsea Market, and a farewell dinner in Chinatown.

activities.name: Greenwich Village Walking Tour
activities.description: Greenwich Village is NYC's bohemian heart — the neighborhood of Bob Dylan, the Stonewall Inn, and Washington Square Park. Start at the iconic Washington Square Arch, watch street performers and NYU students in the park, then wander the tree-lined streets. Every block has character: comedy clubs, jazz bars, tiny bookshops, and some of the best food in the city. The beating heart of the Village. The marble arch was built in 1892 to commemorate George Washington's inauguration. On any given day, you'll find jazz musicians, chess hustlers, dog walkers, and performance artists. It's the most New York scene that isn't a tourist attraction — it's just real city life happening.
details: 💡 The chess tables in the southwest corner are legendary — challenge a local if you dare

activities.name: The High Line
activities.description: This elevated park built on a former freight rail line is one of New York's best urban innovations. Walk the 1.45-mile path from the Meatpacking District to Hudson Yards, passing through gardens, public art installations, and architecture with views of the Hudson River and the city skyline. In April, the spring plantings are just starting to bloom. A block-long food hall in a former Nabisco factory (where the Oreo was invented). Browse dozens of food vendors — from lobster rolls at The Lobster Place to tacos at Los Tacos No. 1. It's also a great spot to pick up souvenirs and gifts. The High Line entrance at 16th Street drops you right at the market.
details: 📍 Enter at Gansevoort Street (south) or 34th Street (north)
⏰ 45-60 minutes end to end, more if you linger
💡 Los Tacos No. 1 is the standout — get the adobada or nopal taco
📍 SoHo: roughly Houston to Canal, Broadway to 6th Ave
💲 Free to browse (your credit card may disagree)
💡 Prince Street Pizza's pepperoni square is famous for a reason
tips: The High Line is best walked south-to-north (Gansevoort → 34th) — you end at Hudson Yards which connects to the subway at 34th Street.

activities.name: Little Italy & Chinatown
activities.description: Walk through what remains of Little Italy (mostly Mulberry Street between Canal and Broome) — it's touristy but the atmosphere is fun for a stroll. Then cross Canal Street into Chinatown, which is vibrant, authentic, and packed with incredible food. The contrast between the two neighborhoods in the span of a block is fascinating. For your last evening, pick your vibe: catch live jazz at Blue Note in Greenwich Village (classic NYC), grab cocktails at a speakeasy like Please Don't Tell (PDT) in the East Village (enter through a phone booth in a hot dog shop), or take in the Manhattan skyline one more time from the East River waterfront.
details: 📍 Mulberry Street (Little Italy) → Canal Street → Mott Street (Chinatown)
💡 Little Italy is mostly for ambiance now — save your appetite for Chinatown
📍 Blue Note: 131 W 3rd St · PDT: 113 St Marks Place
💲 Blue Note: $20-40 cover + drinks · PDT: $16-20 per cocktail
💡 PDT requires a reservation on Resy — book ahead. It's worth the novelty.
tips: For a perfect NYC nightcap, grab a cheesecake from Eileen's Special Cheesecake in SoHo (17 Cleveland Place). Mini cheesecakes, incredible flavors, open late.
